# Kestrel Ridge Coatings: Solvent Transfer and Exposure Protocol

Document SP-118, Revision F. Applies to the Mixing Hall at the Dunmore Road plant. Document owner: Site Environmental, Health and Safety Lead.

## 1. Scope

This protocol governs the transfer of solvents from steel drums into the Mixing Hall day tanks, the exposure limits that apply while doing so, and the response to incidents during a transfer. It applies to employees and contractors alike. Supervisors must confirm that every person on the transfer crew has read this revision before the first transfer of a shift.

> **WARNING:** Toluene and isopropanol drums must never be staged within 4 meters of the hot-melt adhesive line. The line surface runs hot enough to ignite vapor escaping from an open bung.

## 2. Required Protective Equipment

Every crew member wears chemical splash goggles, a face shield during bung removal, nitrile gloves with a minimum thickness of 0.38 mm, and a half-face respirator fitted with organic vapor cartridges. Cartridges are replaced at the end of each shift or after 7 hours of cumulative use, whichever comes first. Respirator fit tests are repeated every 11 months.

## 3. Exposure Limits

The site limits below are stricter than the regulatory limits and take precedence on site. Reaching the action level triggers a mandatory supervisor review of the transfer setup.

| Solvent | 8-hour TWA | 15-minute STEL | Action Level | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Toluene | 18 ppm | 57 ppm | 8.5 ppm | 230 mg/m3 |
| Xylene | 42 ppm | 83 ppm | 21 ppm | 410 mg/m3 |
| Methyl ethyl ketone | 115 ppm | 260 ppm | 55 ppm | 790 mg/m3 |
| n-Butyl acetate | 96 ppm | 145 ppm | 48 ppm | 680 mg/m3 |
| Isopropanol | 175 ppm | 330 ppm | 87 ppm | 920 mg/m3 |

## 4. Transfer Procedure

### 4.1 Pre-Transfer Checks

Confirm the extraction fans are running and the hall reading is below the action level for the solvent being moved. Verify that the spill cart is stocked and positioned at the transfer bay, and that the transfer hose carries a current inspection tag.

### 4.2 Building Ground Verification

Attach the clip to the test lug on the bay wall, then read the meter. The reading must be 25 ohms or lower. If it is higher, tag the bay out of service and notify the maintenance planner.

### 4.3 Drum Bonding Check

Attach the clip to bare metal on the container rim, then read the meter. The reading must be 10 ohms or lower. If it is higher, scrape the contact point clean and test again before any liquid moves.

### 4.4 Pump Transfer

Start the pump at the standard rate of 38 liters per minute and watch the receiving tank level gauge throughout. Stop the pump when the gauge reaches the fill mark; never top off by hand.

> **WARNING:** When transferring methyl ethyl ketone, the pump flow rate must not exceed 19 liters per minute. Faster flow builds static charge more quickly than the bonding system can dissipate it.

## 5. Incident Response

### 5.1 Eye Contact

Flush the affected eye at the nearest eyewash station for 20 minutes while holding the eyelids open, then report to the first aid room.

### 5.2 Re-entry After a Ventilation Alarm

Nobody goes back into the hall until 47 minutes have passed since the extraction fans restarted and a handheld reading below the action level has been logged by the supervisor.

### 5.3 Re-entry After a Spill

Nobody goes back into the hall until 31 minutes have passed since the absorbent material was bagged and sealed and a handheld reading below the action level has been logged by the supervisor.

## 6. Record Keeping

Transfer logs, meter readings and incident reports are kept by the EHS office for 5 years and are available to auditors on request.
